newsitem.title: USA: Ex-CBOE vice chairman to head Chicago trading firm.
newsitem.headline: Ex-CBOE vice chairman to head Chicago trading firm.

text.p: William Floersch, former vice chairman of the Chicago Board Options Exchange, has been named president and chief executive officer of futures and options trading firm O'Connor & Co, the firm said Friday.
The Chicago-based company said Floersch would be responsible for all O'Connor & Co operations.

Floersch will head a management team that will concentrate on expanding the firm's execution and clearing business, with an emphasis on fund managers and other institutional investors, the company said.

Floersch, previously an independent market maker at the CBOE, had stepped down at the end of 1996 after serving six consecutive one-year terms as vice chairman of the exchange. He was also chairman of the CBOE's executive committee.
He had been in the running to succeed CBOE chairman Alger "Duke" Chapman. That job went to William Brodsky, former president of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
